page: Hetzner Cloud ccx13 is a dedicated CPU virtual server instance powered by the QEMU hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads. The hardware allocation includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 3.91 GB per core, alongside 80 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The CPU supports key instruction sets such as AVX, AES, SHA_NI, BMI2, ADX, and FMA, though it lacks AVX-512 and AMX extensions. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPU accelerators are included.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance and overall PassMark CPU scores fall into the bottom 25%, reflecting the physical single-core limitation. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck, with small-block read-only memory bandwidth and PassMark memory scores ranking in the bottom 10%. Large-block write bandwidth and single-threaded compression/decompression tasks (gzip and bzip3) maintain average mid-range performance. Database operations and Redis SET operations show weaker throughput, placing in the bottom 10% and 25% respectively.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ccx13 offers dedicated CPU resources at an entry-level resource density, making it a predictable alternative to shared-core instances without the premium of high-tier compute nodes. The primary tradeoff is the constrained memory bandwidth and limited multi-core scaling. Consequently, this instance is best suited for workloads requiring stable, non-burstable single-threaded CPU performance, such as light web serving, basic text processing, single-threaded utility scripts, and development environments that do not demand high memory throughput or parallel processing.
description: Hetzner Cloud ccx13 is an entry-level dedicated CPU instance featuring an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor with 2 vCPUs (1 physical core, 2 threads) running at 2.0 GHz. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of RAM, 80 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and no GPU. While stress-ng single-core benchmarks indicate strong performance in the top 25%, multi-core metrics and memory bandwidth are significantly constrained, with small-block read-only memory bandwidth and database operations scoring in the bottom 10%. This resource profile offers a qualitative cost-efficient entry point for dedicated CPU access, avoiding the performance fluctuations of shared-core hosts. The ccx13 is best suited for light web serving, text processing, and single-threaded utility workloads that require predictable CPU allocation but do not demand high memory throughput or intensive multi-core parallel processing.
